messages:
mira: Heads-up — I'm starting onboarding for opaline-10b (public checkpoint) for hosted. Initial quant experiments (INT8 groupwise) show QoL regressions and odd token-lag on long ctx (>2k). Also seeing KV-cache eviction spikes when batching. Can we triage what to run first and who owns which checks?

raj: ack. can you paste the minimal repro + the quant recipe you used? important to see whether this is RoPE misalignment or kv eviction policy. also is this only on ded or hosted?

mira: repro below. ran our standard qconfig: --quant method=groupwise int8 --perchannel false --clip-values true. repro is on dedicated dev pool (A100). Hosted smoke replicates at small scale too. log snippet: ```
[2024-11-03 14:02:12] request_id=abcd1234 seq=0 tokens=512 kv_miss=0.87 latency=120ms
[2024-11-03 14:02:13] request_id=abcd1235 seq=1 tokens=512 kv_miss=0.12 latency=30ms
[2024-11-03 14:02:13] WARNING: rotary_kv_angle_mismatch detected for layer 10
```

lucas: interesting — that mix of high then low kv_miss suggests eviction thrashing during batching. also the rotary angle warning is suspicious. quick checklist: 1) baseline full-fp32 run for logits+perplexity 2) reproduce quant run with kv-logging enabled 3) run rope alignment probe (small script) 4) run batch size sweep to surface eviction breakpoints.

anya: I can run the quant eval for the 1M prompt subset today. will compare perplexity + topk jitter vs fp32. assign to me.

kevin: i'll take runtime side — enable continuous kv metrics on the dedicated pool and run batch sweep. can we add a small smoke route to the canary with fallback to fp16? if we see threshold breaches we can auto-fallback. ops-bot, can you spin a canary slot?

ops-bot: @kevin Canary slot c-opa-01 provisioned in us-west2; env=dedicated-dev; route=/v1/models/opaline-10b/smoke. max qps=10. logs forwarded to /infra/logs/opaline-canary.

raj: for the rope probe, use this quick check: ```python
# rope-check.py (toy)
from model_utils import load, run
mdl = load('opaline-10b', dtype='fp32')
res = run(mdl, input='The quick brown fox'*80, record_rotary_angles=True)
print(res.rotary_angle_stats())
```
we've seen angle resync on adapters when quant kernels reorder matmuls.

mira: thanks. prioritization: P1 for customer-facing routes (we have one prod customer on dedicated path). propose this plan: (A) reproduce and confirm whether issue is quant or runtime (B) if quant, try per-channel and symmetric quant fallback (C) if runtime, patch batching/eviction thresholds + add auto-fallback. timeline: aim EOD triage + next-day mitigation.

lucas: +1. add a quick unit test that fails on known-bad prompt (short seq then long). i'll PR the rope probe and a small kv-metrics exporter.

anya: running eval now, will post perplexity diffs here in ~3h.

kevin: i'll start batch sweep now. first check: batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16] with kv-cache warmup=2. will post results.

mira: assigning owners: mira (triage lead), anya (quant eval), kevin (runtime), lucas (probe + tests), raj (follow up on model/quant config). returning to thread with results. please ping if blocked. :thumbsup:

kevin: quick interim finding — at batch>=8 kv_eviction_rate jumps >0.6 after 200 steps, and latency spikes. looks like our batching heuristic doesn't account for grouping behavior in the new model. attaching mini-csv.

mira: good catch. can we try reducing batch token cap and enabling strict kv retention for first 4 layers? that often helps with rotary-angle drift.

lucas: i'll push a runtime flag kv_strict_layers=[0,1,2,3] behind a feature flag on canary.

ops-bot: deploy started for canary c-opa-01 (build=2024.11.03-2245). watch: https://ci.internal/deploys/2245

anya: eval update: FP32 ppl=14.2, INT8 groupwise ppl=16.8 (+18% relative), INT8 per-channel ppl=14.5 (~+2% rel). topk jitter higher on groupwise. attaching small table.

mira: that pretty much points to quant scheme. action: switch to per-channel quant for production until we have a groupwise kernel fix. kevin/lucas — rollback plan on canary if we see error rate >0.5% in 1h.

kevin: will monitor and auto-fallback if errors breach. setting alert now.

mira: thanks team. will create intake ticket with links to logs and attach these outputs. closing initial triage thread — followups in ticket #IN-3821.

raj: great work. leave here for async updates. :rocket:
